A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same contamination-detection survey. All 23 pages of v4 and 28 pages of v5, including figures, tables, equations and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: v4 presents a literature survey and taxonomy. Its experimental outcomes, including controlled training and membership-inference results, are attributed to cited studies.

after.justification: v5 remains a survey without original empirical results. The additional benchmark findings are attributed to other studies, and Table 3 provides conceptual classification rather than experimental measurements.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an executable detection algorithm or model. The added descriptions of memorization and soft-prompting methods concern cited research, not changes to a method developed by this work.

E1.justification: Neither survey actually trains or evaluates models on datasets. v5 adds discussion of GSM-Plus, MATH-Perturb, LiveBench and Chatbot Arena in Section 5.3, expanding literature coverage without adding datasets used experimentally by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. New methods appearing in the survey and classification tables are reviewed literature, not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No evaluation protocol is implemented by either survey. Retained experimental descriptions preserve their settings; newly described benchmark construction procedures belong to cited studies.

E4.justification: Neither version conducts ablations, robustness experiments or error analyses. v5 adds summaries of published perturbation studies and conceptual training-stage guidance, without performing new supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests for original empirical analysis. Existing statistical statements attributed to surveyed studies remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v5 adds secondary findings, including relative performance drops above 30% on GSM-Plus and Carlini et al.'s observations linking memorization to model size, data frequency and prompt length. Retained numerical summaries, including Min-K% Prob's 0.72 ROC-AUC, are unchanged. These are newly summarized published results, not new experiments by the survey authors.

T1.justification: New Section 2 introduces formal definitions of contamination using a similarity threshold, membership inference as a binary function, and memorization through a probability comparison. v4 provides informal explanations and set-intersection notation. The existing Min-K formulas are retained and renumbered; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The introduction moderates the novelty claim from being the first thorough survey to being one of the first, and increases claimed coverage from more than 100 to more than 120 relevant papers. The abstract, detection-focused purpose and principal taxonomy contributions remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 and Table 3 add substantial guidance on suitability across pre-training, instruction-tuning and RLHF, including a warning that RLHF can weaken confidence-based contamination signals. v5 also distinguishes membership inference from contamination, expands contamination-source explanations, and develops specific scalability, adversarial-evasion, legal and privacy challenges beyond v4's brief discussion.

D1.justification: Section 1.2 newly discloses an inclusive literature-selection policy covering relevant open-access papers regardless of publication status, predominantly from 2023–2025. This provides limited additional reproducibility information about the survey; no implementation or code-access resources are added.

R1.justification: v5 adds literature on memorization, soft prompting, benchmark perturbation, dynamic evaluation and proposed future directions. Section 1.3 expands the comparison with Deng, Palavalli and Fu while retaining the survey's overall positioning. The new MATH-Perturb passage has a citation mismatch: Huang et al. (2023) corresponds to C-Eval in the bibliography.

P1.justification: The introduction gains subsections, contributions and related-survey discussion are reorganized, and the discussion separates open pre-training data from other benchmarks. Dedicated definitions and practical-usage sections improve navigation. Most existing method-review prose and the abstract retain their wording.

P2.justification: v5 adds the training-stage classification in Table 3 and extends Figure 1 and Table 2 with Carlini et al. and Dynamic Soft Prompting. Table 2 also receives reordered entries and an expanded caption. Publication headers and float placement change, while Table 1 and the overall visual format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 makes the survey more useful through clearer positioning, explicit conceptual definitions, and practical training-stage guidance with applicability cautions. These address gaps in v4's explanatory treatment while retaining its substantive review. The new MATH-Perturb citation mismatch weakens traceability, but the overall gains in clarity and guidance support a limited net improvement.
